### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **20** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `187705f6348f215b18c2a95a9f211265cc85c18f` — the merge of head `2e8ba4089ac9fdde45d75931093217b2becd88cb` into base `06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 187705f6348f215b18c2a95a9f211265cc85c18f && git checkout 187705f6348f215b18c2a95a9f211265cc85c18f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924 2e8ba4089ac9fdde45d75931093217b2becd88cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924 && git merge --no-ff 2e8ba4089ac9fdde45d75931093217b2becd88cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 06881565bdced6c949f05d59f0059a3ff7409924
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2e8ba4089ac9fdde45d75931093217b2becd88cb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.text-object-value.test.ts, packages/rest/src/engine-sqlite-text-object-value.test.ts + packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts (`STRING_VALUE_TYPES`, `valueSchemaFor`), packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts (`BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`, `defaultValue`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`insert` / `update` doors, `resolveNowDefault`, `normalizeExpressionDefault`), packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/core/src/utils/import-coerce.ts, packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts (`xlsxCellToString`), packages/core/src/utils/required-emptiness.ts

Inputs read: card #29645 (body, triage 6591873816, claim 6592073199, os-dev-report 6592841327), PR #29684 (body, 4-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's 45 check-runs. The changeset `.changeset/29645-text-field-refuses-any-object.md` is read for ② only, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing, one hunk.** `validateOne`'s `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES` arm replaces `isPlainObjectValue(value) || Array.isArray(value)` with `isObjectValue(value)` (the #29562 helper, `typeof value === 'object' && value !== null`) and names the shape with the existing `receivedObjectShape`. Net effect on the twelve types (`text`, `textarea`, `email`, `url`, `phone`, `password`, `markdown`, `html`, `richtext`, `code`, `signature`, `qrcode`): a `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, class instance, typed array or any other non-plain object is now refused `invalid_type` / `invalid_value_shape` with `expected a string, received an object`; a plain object and an array keep the refusal they already had, with the identical code, message key and detail. **Right** — this is exactly the card's Wanted 2 (same helper, no copy), and `receivedObjectShape` gives the same `an object` / `an array` words the old inline ternary did.
2. **Ordering.** The test sits where the old one sat: after the `required` / `isMissing` gate and the #5922 filter-operator refusal, before `if (shapeOnly) return null`, so a readonly field's value is judged under `validateRecordInScope(..., 'include')` and a `{ $in: [...] }` keeps its own sentence. **Right**; pinned by the readonly case and the "leaves alone" block.
3. **`email` / `url` / `phone` answer changes** from `invalid_email` / `invalid_url` / `invalid_phone` to `invalid_type` for these shapes, because the shape test now runs ahead of the format regex. **Right** and declared in the changeset (the old code was an accident of `String(value)` failing the regex, as the live arm's own comment on #5922 already says for the operator-object case).
4. **`isPlainObjectValue` keeps one caller** (the `currency` arm's sentence choice at the live tree's line 1452) so no unused-helper lint arises; its docblock still describes that role. **Right**.
5. **`normalizeNumericStringValues` is untouched** at the door; only its "not touched" docblock paragraph is reworded. A number or boolean keeps #29241 (written as its string, then judged); a Date is left as sent and refused by the arm. **Right**; pinned (`toBe(row)` identity and the `'42'` SQLite control).
6. **Public surface**: no export, type, schema key or wire code added or removed; the existing `invalid_type` code and `invalid_value_shape` catalog key are reused, so no i18n bundle moves. `normalizeBlankTypedRow` (the #29343 serial constraint) is not in the diff. **Right**.
7. **Reach claim** ("REST over JSON sees no change"): a JSON body cannot carry these shapes; the XLSX import flattens every cell to a string in `xlsxCellToString` (`packages/rest/src/import-prepare.ts`, a `Date` to its naive wall-clock text) before `coerceFieldValue`, and the CSV path is strings by construction. So the only doors that change are the engine's `insert` / `insertMany` / `update` by id / `update` by predicate / `validate()` dry run (the `engine-validate.ts` path runs the same validator), from flows, hooks and server code. **Right**; the pins cover insert, insertMany, both update forms and the readonly scope.
8. **Tests**: the objectql pin reads the twelve-member set from `@objectstack/spec/data` and pins its membership by name, so a future member joins the loop and the name pin reds; the rest pin reads the physical SQLite column through the driver's query builder, the same `(driver as any).knex` convention `rest-data-number-value.test.ts` and `rest-data-blank-typed-value.test.ts` already use. **Right**.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29645-text-field-refuses-any-object.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`, title with `!`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a BREAKING banner with Before / Now / Unchanged and the remedy. The diff publishes only `@objectstack/objectql` (the rest file is a test and publishes nothing). Metadata-protocol `none` is right: no schema key, accepted metadata value or type moves, and `defaultValue` literals were already bound by `valueSchemaFor` (`z.string()`), so no author-written metadata is newly refused. By AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3 a `none` kind takes `patch`, keeping the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 disposition: **matches**. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the reading #29133's changeset used for the identical class of change and the card's Level line names. **Right**. The `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` check-runs on the head are `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in os-dev-report 6592841327 — nothing to answer.
- Deviations flagged by the dev: (a) branch name `claude/project-thread-pcnric` instead of `claude/issue-29645-slug` — a naming deviation of the card-thread mode, no contract effect; (b) no separate dogfood case although the claim's file surface named one — the recording-driver pin in objectql and the real-SqlDriver pin in rest cover every engine door the card names and the full dogfood battery is reported green, so the reach is pinned; **answered, not a gap**; (c) harness attribution comment and template headings in the PR body — prose, outside scope.
- No dev flag names a design doubt. No `security_findings`, no `out_of_scope_findings`.
- Ruling check: the card is a self-declared follow-up S4 of the #29562 contract review; its Wanted 1-3 and Level line are all met by the diff (measurement table in the PR body and both pin headers; refusal via the shared helper; per-type pins plus a per-type plain-string control). No maintainer ruling on the card contradicts the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing read against the published spec on `main`:

- `valueSchemaFor` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`) returns `z.string()` for every member of `STRING_VALUE_TYPES`, which contains all twelve `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`. The spec's stored value for this class is one string; a `Date`, `Map`, `Set`, class instance or typed array is already refused by the spec's own contract. The record validator admitting them on a `String(value)` reading was an implementation gap at the consumer, and the diff **makes the spec's own refusal real**: nothing declared is taken away.
- I tried to find a declared producer that hands one of these shapes to a text-family field and would now be broken: a `defaultValue` literal must satisfy `valueSchemaFor` at parse time (`field.zod.ts` line 1386), so a `Date` literal cannot be declared; a CEL default that evaluates to a `Date` goes through `normalizeExpressionDefault` -> `resolveNowDefault(fieldType, …)`, which returns the ISO string for any non-`date`/`time` type, so a `now()`-style default on a text field lands as a string, not a `Date`; the XLSX and CSV imports flatten cells to strings before coercion; REST JSON carries none. The one real reach is server code, hooks and flows (`update_record` spreads authored fields), where before the change SQLite stored a `Date` as its epoch number in TEXT and a `Map` or `Set` as `"{}"` — a corrupt stored value, never a capability. The remedy the changeset gives (`toISOString()`, `JSON.stringify`, or declare `datetime` / `json`) is the correct one.
- Boundary cases probed: `required` + object — `isEmptyForRequired` (core) treats any present non-array value as non-empty, so the object reaches the arm and gets `invalid_type`, not `required`; `null` and a missing key still stop at `isMissing`; a filter-operator object keeps its #5922 sentence; a `json` field stays open (`z.unknown()`), pinned. The `currency` arm's `isPlainObjectValue` call is a sentence choice and is rightly untouched.
- Shape of the change: the string arm now shares one object predicate with the option arms (#29562), so the two families that store a string cannot drift apart again; the typed `value is object` guard feeds `receivedObjectShape(value: object)` without a cast.

Findings: no must-fix. No should-fix inside the diff. Out of scope, noted not filed: `color` and `secret` are in `STRING_VALUE_TYPES` but outside `BOUNDED_STRING_FIELD_TYPES`, so the record validator has no string arm for them at all; the same `Date`-on-a-string-field question exists there and is neither this card's Wanted nor touched by this diff.

Gates: every check-run on the head has completed; 35 `success` (Test Core 1-8 and the aggregate, Build Core, all Type Check and Lint families, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes), the rest `skipped` by their path filters; zero `failure`, zero `cancelled`. Docs Drift Check lists no page (no hand-written page names the derived anchor); a `git grep` of `content/docs` for the text-family value contract finds no page that states a non-string value on a text field is stringified, so no prose is falsified.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-pcnric`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbXKRzgnVvjzxaYxLUf`

**VERDICT: PASS**
